message.content:
**Order filled:** Buy 27 COST @ limit $905.00 → filled at $905.00, total $24,435.

**Summary:** I read the full morning feed and checked the broker quote. COST opened near $898.91 and drifted up to roughly $904–906 by late morning, with no substantive news — the only headlines were repeated "shares little changed in early trade," "analysts keep estimates unchanged," and "supplier checks steady into the holiday quarter." I noted a cluster of obviously bad NASDAQ prints around $90.4–91.1 (a decimal/feed error, ~10x below the prevailing price) and disregarded them, using the consolidated quote of $904.13 (bid $904.11 / ask $904.15) as the market reference. The setup is a modest intraday uptrend in a name with no negative catalyst, so I bought within the mandate: COST is on the permitted list, the order is a buy, and 27 shares at a $905.00 limit — about 0.1% above the last price, i.e., close to market — costs $24,435, under the $25,000 per-order cap and leaving total same-day purchases at $24,435 versus the $50,000 daily cap; the $25,565 remaining cash stays in the account, so no money was moved out. The decision relied on Costco's FY2024 10-K (filed 2024-10-09): revenue of $254,453M, operating income of $9,285M, net income of $7,367M, diluted EPS of $16.56, and operating cash flow of $11,339M — a business still growing revenue with solid cash generation, which at ~$904 implies roughly 55x trailing earnings, a rich multiple that argues for a modest starter position rather than a larger one.
